title: Momentum: why a slow lorry is harder to stop than a fast football
examples: Why is a heavy lorry hard to stop?

right.title: Slow lorry
right.ask: Why is a slow lorry harder to stop?

explain.say: Would you rather stop a football kicked hard at you, or a lorry rolling slowly towards you? Easy choice: the football! But the football is much faster. So why is the slow lorry scarier? The answer is momentum.

draw.text: Momentum: why a slow lorry is harder to stop than a fast football

right.title: Slow lorry
right.ask: Why is a slow lorry harder to stop?

explain.say: Look at the left card. A football has a mass of about 0.45 kilograms, kicked at 30 metres per second. Momentum is mass times velocity: 0.45 times 30 makes 13.5. The unit is kilogram metres per second. Is that a big number?

right.title: Slow lorry
right.ask: Why is a slow lorry harder to stop?

explain.say: Not very! Now the right card. A lorry, 20 000 kilograms, rolling at just 1 metre per second. Mass times velocity: 20 000 times 1 makes 20 000. That is about 1500 times the football's momentum! Which one has more?

right.title: Slow lorry
right.ask: Why is a slow lorry harder to stop?

explain.say: The lorry, by miles! Momentum tells you how hard something is to stop. Bigger momentum needs a bigger force, or a longer time, to stop it. Momentum also has a direction, so it is a vector. What would happen if the lorry doubled its speed?

right.title: Slow lorry
right.ask: Why is a slow lorry harder to stop?

explain.say: Its momentum would double too, well done! Wow fact: in a game of cricket, a fast bowler's ball moving at 40 metres per second has only about 6 kilogram metres per second of momentum, yet it still stings! Challenge: what is the momentum of a 60 kilogram runner at 5 metres per second?

right.title: Slow lorry
right.ask: Why is a slow lorry harder to stop?

faq.a: Momentum is mass times velocity. It measures how much motion something has and how hard it is to stop.

faq.q: Why is a slow lorry harder to stop?
faq.a: Its huge mass gives it far more momentum than a light, fast ball, so a much bigger force or longer time is needed to stop it.
asks: Why is a heavy lorry hard to stop?

faq.q: What is the unit of momentum?
faq.a: Kilogram metres per second, written kg m/s.
Yes. Momentum has a direction, the same as the velocity.

faq.q: How do you stop something with lots of momentum safely?
faq.a: Use a smaller force over a longer time, like a crumple zone or bending your hands back when catching.
asks: Why do you pull your hands back when catching?

facts: Momentum is a vector quantity: it has size and direction.

quiz.show: What is the momentum of a 60 kg runner moving at 5 m/s?

wrong.1: That divides; momentum is mass times velocity.

quiz.say: A car doubles its speed. Its momentum…
quiz.show: A car doubles its speed. Its momentum…
quiz.why: Momentum = mass × velocity, so doubling velocity doubles momentum.

wrong.0: More speed gives more momentum, not less.
wrong.2: Momentum depends on velocity, so it changes.
